title: Tahini vs. peanut butter

seo.title: Tahini vs. peanut butter: nutrition comparison
seo.meta_description: Per 30 g, tahini has ~209 calories, 5.9 g protein and 107 mg magnesium; peanut butter ~177 calories, 7.2 g protein and 58 mg magnesium.
seo.search_intent: Compare tahini and peanut butter for protein, fat, fiber, calories and minerals

excerpt: At an equal 30 g serving, the tahini reference provides about 209 calories, 5.9 g protein, 18.7 g fat, 2.5 g fiber and 107 mg magnesium. Peanut butter provides about 177 calories, 7.2 g protein, 14.8 g fat, 1.9 g fiber and 58 mg magnesium. Peanut butter leads in protein; tahini stands out for iron and magnesium, although brands can shift the result.
content_html:
Tahini and peanut butter play similar kitchen roles: a spoonful can transform toast, a sauce or a bowl. Nutritionally, however, the tahini reference is fattier and richer in several minerals, while peanut butter provides more protein for the same weight.

Compare 30 g with 30 g

Per 30 gTahiniPeanut butter
Calories~209~177
Protein~5.9 g~7.2 g
Fat~18.7 g~14.8 g
Fiber~2.5 g~1.9 g
Magnesium~107 mg~58 mg
Iron~2.1 mg~0.6 mg
Calcium~35 mg~15 mg

These are two specific USDA Foundation references, not every jar on the market. Added oil, sugar and salt can alter a commercial product.

For protein: peanut butter

The peanut-butter reference contains about 24 g protein/100 g versus 19.7 g in tahini. At 30 g, the difference is around 1.3 g—real, but not enormous.

For magnesium and iron: tahini

Tahini provides about 357 mg magnesium and 7 mg iron/100 g, compared with roughly 193 mg and 1.85 mg in peanut butter. The difference remains meaningful in a normal serving.

Calcium is more complicated than the sesame reputation suggests

Tahini leads these references, but at a relatively modest 116 mg calcium/100 g versus about 50 mg in peanut butter. An unhulled sesame paste could produce a different result because the hull contains much of the seed's calcium.

Calories differ because fat differs

The tahini reference contains about 32 more calories per 30 g, largely because it has more total fat. In a teaspoon the absolute difference is small; in a 50–60 g sauce it becomes easier to notice.

Which should you choose?

Peanut butter if protein and peanut flavor are priorities; tahini if sesame flavor, magnesium or iron matter more. For either one, a simple ingredient list makes the comparison about the seed or peanut rather than added sugar and oils.

faq.question: Which has more protein, tahini or peanut butter?
faq.answer: Peanut butter in these references: about 24 versus 19.7 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more magnesium?
faq.answer: Tahini: about 357 mg/100 g versus 193 mg in peanut butter.

faq.question: Which has more calories?
faq.answer: Tahini in these references: about 697 versus 589 calories/100 g.

faq.question: Do all brands compare the same way?
faq.answer: No. Added salt, sugar, oils and the type of sesame can change the numbers.
